decisions.resolution: 'Great Britain' wins in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading and legend, arrivalDate labels by state, proposedPlaceOfLanding hint, confirmation body; the dashboard intro names no territory today — guidance-before-you-start) and the service applies no nation or territory check to the placeOfDestination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service. The SI's England-only drafting is recorded as a legal note on the england-vs-great-britain behaviour, not rendered and not built.
decisions.rationale: Outside the SI's operative clauses the policy paper is GB throughout: section:policy/para:2 ('into GB'), para:6/item:1-2 ('arrival in GB'), para:7 (APHA, FC or Scottish Government spot-check at destination), section:summary/para:4 (all three need access), annex:6/functional/item:11 (SG and FC get the same access as APHA); and the SI's own destination clause reg 26(2)(b) says 'intended destination in Great Britain' — a consignment landing in England may be bound for Scotland or Wales and is still notified. The tier-2 sources are unanimous: every NNS-UN Applies-to cell is 'EU > GB', the mural service card is 'High risk Plants EU -> GB', and both the Confluence requirements page (h4:All other goods/li:1) and the mural data-fields board (file:data-fields/region:Other goods/item:1) transcribe reg 26(2)(a) itself as 'landing in GB ... arrived in Great Britain' (verified in the extracts). No source asks the notifier to state or prove the nation of arrival, so a territorial check would invent an obligation; either string is feature copy, so the engine imposes nothing. The spec already carries Great Britain on arrivalStatus.label, the arrival-status page title, arrivalDate.input.labelByState and proposedPlaceOfLanding.hint; the one thing it does not yet say is that the destination address is not territorially checked.

decisions.resolution: Collect exactly the statutory matters: one arrivalDate for every commodity type; arrivalTime only when commodityType = potatoes; arrivalStatus only for plants-for-planting and wood-and-cut-trees. A potato notification is always framed as pre-arrival ('Expected date of arrival'), a past date is accepted and flagged late by lateNotificationIndicator, never rejected, and no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes; the arrival-status page needs no authored gate because the derived gate hides it for potatoes.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(2)(a) 'the expected time and date of their arrival' is the only potato timing matter and reg 24A has no post-arrival branch; reg 26(2)(a) branches ('or, if the consignment has arrived in England, the date on which it first arrived') and has no time. h4:Potatoes (seed and ware)/li:1, h4:All other goods/li:1, file:data-fields/region:Potatoes/item:1 and region:Other goods/item:1 restate the same split, so there is nothing to adjudicate — only a gap for late potatoes, which file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2 proves exist and section:non-compliance/para:2 treats as a non-compliance to manage, not a reason to refuse. Inventing a potato already-arrived matter would add a question no source asks (NNS-UN-010 proportionate; Article 9(7) OCR strictly-necessary, section:legal-basis/para:1). NNS-UN-035 (one date field whose meaning switches) is met by arrivalDate.labelByState. Engine: both gates are top-level scalar gates on commodityType (equalsGate for arrivalTime, includesGate for arrivalStatus), same frame, wipeOnExit by the evaluator; the arrival-status page collects only arrivalStatus so pageGatePasses fails for potatoes by the derived rule (skeleton derived-gates) — the spec's page.gate currently holds a prose string an implementor may read as an authored gate, and should be null. The one service-design gap is the label 'Expected date of arrival' shown to somebody whose potatoes arrived yesterday: a hint line resolves it without a new matter.

decisions.resolution: The importer selects arrivalStatus on its own single-question page (plants and wood only, radios Yes first) before arrival-details and place-of-destination; the service never derives it from the date. Because the SI's two either/ors are not the same condition — the date turns on 'arrived in England', the location on 'arrived at its intended destination' — the destination page's already-arrived copy tells a notifier whose consignment has landed but not reached its destination to give the intended destination, so one binary status serves both clauses.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(a)-(b) frame arrival as a fact the operator states ('if the consignment has arrived'), and NNS-UN-036 ('based on the current status of my consignment'), NNS-UN-001 and NNS-UN-025 ('pre-nots'/'post-nots') treat it as something the importer knows; NNS-UN-010 is met because it is a single radio, not a data matter. Deriving from arrivalDate is wrong on the day of arrival and for an expected date that has slipped, and would make the destination page's copy depend on a clock read rather than an answer — which the model cannot express and the copy tripwires cannot pin; one-thing-per-page favours a discrete radios page, and the derived gate hides it for potatoes at no cost. Reg 26(2)(b)'s condition is 'arrived at its intended destination in Great Britain', so a consignment that has landed and is in transit must give the intended destination — 'Where is the consignment now?' alone would mislead — and a hint covers it without a third state. Yes first: animals' own yes/no radios read 'Yes | No' (live-animals extract, regionOfOriginCodeRequirement and containsUnweanedAnimals) and the GOV.UK Design System's yes/no examples lead with Yes; an order-only edit with no model change. The spec already matches the pick otherwise.

decisions.resolution: arrivalDate validates as a real calendar date (dateText) with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds; the single bound is sourced — when arrivalStatus = already-arrived the date may not be after today in Europe/London (dateTextInRange, max only) because it is 'the date on which it first arrived' — and the picker carries data-max-date only in that state and no data-min-date in any state. Expected dates (potatoes, not-yet-arrived) accept any past or future date; lateness is computed, never validated; a typo sanity window is parked, not built.
decisions.rationale: No plants source bounds the date: the timing rules are relative to it (section:policy/para:6; annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)), annex:6/functional/item:2 and section:non-compliance/para:2 require a late notification to be accepted, and file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2 needs a past date. Animals' [today - 7 days, today + 6 months] (live-animals arrivalDateAtPort validationRaw; arrival.js:5) would reject the mural late-potato fixture whenever the lorry arrived more than a week ago — a plants-source reason to diverge under standing ruling 5. The already-arrived ceiling is the SI's own semantics (reg 26(2)(a)) and stops a self-contradictory answer (already arrived, future date) that would also make the lateness rule nonsense; it can never refuse a lawful notification because a consignment that has arrived has arrived today or earlier. A one-year-each-way sanity window has no source — its numbers would be a policy answer nobody has (standing ruling 1) — and a picker min/max would display a rule the regulation does not impose; it is parked. Engine: dateTextInRange takes optional min and max (lib/validate/validators.js:269-271 — verified, max alone works), the bounds helper beside arrival-details returns { max, maxText } from one clock read (skeleton date-fields; docs/validation.md), and the controller builds the schema in POST from answers.arrivalStatus as it already does for scope.has() fields. No model change.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge (sanity window [today - 1 year, today + 1 year] with the bounds named in the error): lost because the numbers have no source and standing ruling 1 parks a policy answer nobody has — typo protection is parked, not rejected. Policy judge (no bound at all, no picker attributes): lost on the already-arrived ceiling because reg 26(2)(a)'s 'date on which it first arrived' cannot be a future date, the engineering judge showed dateTextInRange takes max alone, and the ceiling cannot refuse a lawful notification.

decisions.resolution: The SI wording wins: plants and wood may be notified before arrival or no later than four days after the date of arrival; potatoes only before, at least two days before the expected date. Lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London and ignores arrivalTime — potatoes are late when the notification day is after arrivalDate minus 2 days, plants and wood when it is after arrivalDate plus 4 days (notifying on arrivalDate minus 2, or on arrivalDate plus 4, is on time); a future date can still be late for potatoes but never for plants and wood, and the windows are shown up front as option hints on commodity-type and per state on arrival-status.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1) 'before or no later than four days after the date of their arrival' is the only text that explicitly admits a pre-arrival plants notification and reg 26(2)(a) presupposes it; section:policy/para:6/item:2 is a shorter restatement of the same rule, not a contradiction, and standing ruling 4 gives the SI precedence in any case. Reg 24A(1) 'at least two days before the expected date of their arrival' counts by date, so the unit is the calendar day and the potato time (reg 24A(2)(a)) is a matter to record, not part of the deadline — recorded as a provisional reading. NNS-UN-001/025/036's generic pre/post vocabulary is consistent with the split and supplies no commodity rule of its own. The spec is inconsistent with itself: the commodity-type page notes and the adopted guidance-link-not-in-journey-pages behaviour promise per-option timing hints but commodityType carries no valueHints (verified). The calendar helpers startOfDayInZone, startOfUtcDay and addUtcDays exist in lib/validate/calendar.js (verified), so the rule is a pure function with no new library code.

decisions.resolution: After submission the late highlight is shown in three places — a govukNotificationBanner naming the rule breached on the confirmation page and on the SUBMITTED read-only check-your-answers view, and a Late tag beside the status on the dashboard card; before submission the DRAFT check-your-answers page shows govukWarningText when the entered date would make the notification late if submitted today, computed by the same helper with the request clock, and says it can still be submitted. It never blocks and there is no separate late page. lateNotificationIndicator is a manifest obligation with system: true, listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED: one pure helper computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) and is called twice — with the request clock for the DRAFT check-your-answers warning, and with the finalise clock in the declaration POST, whose result is committed as a system value in fulfilment immediately before submitJourney only when the journey is DRAFT (c-030); confirmation, the submitted check-your-answers view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from submittedAt.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/functional/item:2 'Highlight to the user (internal and external) when a notification was made outside of required timings' is past tense and names both audiences: the confirmation banner and read-only CYA serve the notifier and the stored submittedAt plus answers serve the regulator (NNS-UN-014); NNS-UN-012 wants the rule named, not just 'late'; section:non-compliance/para:2 lists late notification among non-compliances managed by advice, warnings or sanctions, so submission proceeds. No source asks for a pre-submission warning and the policy judge saw a trade-off; the panel builds it because NNS-UN-007 (confidence the information is correct, avoid errors) and NNS-UN-012 ('so that I can meet the rules') are both served by telling the notifier before they commit, a mistyped date is exactly what CYA exists to catch, the commodity-type hints already name the rule so the warning reveals nothing new, the Design System's warning text exists for something the user needs to know before continuing, and the engineering judge showed it is the same pure helper with a different clock argument — one component on an existing page, no engine change. Engine: submitJourney is records.finalise and nothing else (engine/write/submit.js — verified) and checks only recognised keys and readiness, so the declaration controller commits the helper's result as a system value before calling it and a system value no page collects never blocks; the backend and the stub re-stamp submittedAt on every submission and keep no first-submission timestamp (stub/lifecycle/transition.js:14, :32, :47; NotificationAggregate.submittedAt), which is why the flag is stored at the first finalise from DRAFT rather than derived from submittedAt (c-030 — Amend is in scope); the boot guard requires a system obligation to be listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED (boot-guards-three); the mapper has no typed home (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/limits.md), so the flag travels in the opaque fulfilments payload with an explicit omission assertion on the NotificationDto. No finalise hook and no engine change.
decisions.dissent: Policy judge: park the pre-submission warning — no source asks for it and it may deter a late-but-needed notification or invite an 'incorrect notification details' non-compliance by nudging the date. Lost 2-1: the warning copy says the notification can still be submitted, the rule is already visible on commodity-type so nothing new is revealed, NNS-UN-007 and NNS-UN-012 favour telling the notifier before they commit, and it costs one component on an existing page.

decisions.resolution: Build it in the first pass as a stored system value: a pure lateness helper beside the check-answers feature computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) using the c-031 calendar-day rule; the declaration POST calls it with the finalise clock and commits the result as the lateNotificationIndicator system value (manifest obligation, system: true, in SYSTEM_POPULATED) immediately before submitJourney when the journey is DRAFT, leaving it untouched on a re-submit from AMEND (c-030); the draft CYA calls the same helper with the request clock for its warning; confirmation, the submitted CYA and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value (c-035). No finalise hook, no backend field, no engine change.
decisions.rationale: Sourced by section:policy/para:6/item:1-2, annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1), annex:6/functional/item:2, NNS-UN-012 and NNS-UN-014. The four open points the reconciler listed all close with the engine as it is: calendar days because the SI measures from a date and the potato time does not enter the deadline (c-031); warn on the draft CYA with the same helper (c-035); the engine-hook-versus-backend question dissolves because submitJourney is finalise only and checks only recognised keys and readiness (engine/write/submit.js), so the declaration controller commits the helper's result as a system value before calling it — no hook, and no read-time derivation from submittedAt, which the backend and stub re-stamp on every submission (stub/lifecycle/transition.js:14,32; c-030); the mapper has no typed home (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/limits.md), so the flag gets an explicit omission assertion rather than a payload property. The calendar helpers already exist, so the increment is one helper with a unit test, copy in both languages and three render sites — standing ruling 1: buildable now. Residual parked: projecting the flag into the backend NotificationDto for the regulator side (Mapper A has no field); the backend receives the opaque fulfilments carrying the stored flag and can project it later.

decisions.resolution: Build the user-selected arrivalStatus radios page (Yes first) for plants and wood, placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination; potatoes have no status and skip the page by the derived gate. The service never derives the status from the date, in this run or later.
decisions.rationale: Per c-006: annex:5/reg:26(2)(a)-(b) make the branch a fact about the consignment the operator declares, and NNS-UN-036, NNS-UN-001 and NNS-UN-025 treat it as something the importer states; the day-of-arrival case is undecidable from a date. Engine: arrivalStatus is a top-level scalar with includesGate on commodityType (helpers/index.js), same frame, wipeOnExit by the evaluator; the page collects one in-scope obligation so the derived gate (flow/gates.js; skeleton derived-gates) hides it for potatoes and the opening run skips it — single-question recipe, one increment, no authored gate. The arrival-status page already exists in the spec with the right pattern (legend as heading, caption Arrival).

decisions.resolution: Build with 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string and no nation check on the destination address. The residual legal question — whether the draft SI is widened to GB or Scottish and Welsh instruments mirror it, and whether a Scottish or Welsh destination ever routes elsewhere — is recorded as PARKED (policy) inside this behaviour and changes no page.
decisions.rationale: The buildable half is settled at c-001 from the policy paper's own GB wording (section:policy/para:6; annex:5/reg:26(2)(b)), para:7 and annex:6/functional/item:11 (Scottish Government is a competent authority with full access) and the unanimous tier-2 'EU > GB' framing, and three pages (arrival-status, arrival-details, place-of-destination) need that rule now. The residual is a policy answer nobody has — the draft SI says 'into England' (reg 24A(1), reg 26(1)) and the paper contains no Scottish or Welsh instrument — so under standing ruling 1 it is parked, not rejected and not built; it gates no increment because the service collects the same matters whichever nation the consignment lands in, placeOfDestination has no nation field to validate, and NNS-UN-029 is served by the destination address rather than by asking the notifier anything extra. Recording the residual as PARKED inside an adopted behaviour keeps one status per behaviour (spec-set-behaviour-status.sh accepts adopted | open-question | parked | rejected) and leaves the pages an adopted rule to cite.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge: park the behaviour as a whole because what remains is a legislative question. Lost 2-1 on labelling only — the copy convention and the no-validation rule are built now, and parking the whole behaviour would leave three pages' copy without an adopted rule to cite; the residual is recorded as PARKED in the detail.

decisions.resolution: Build arrivalDate as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no picker min/max, except a maximum of today when arrivalStatus = already-arrived, from one bounds helper beside arrival-details. A past expected date for potatoes does not trigger an arrived question — potatoes have no arrived state — it is accepted, the potato hint says what to enter, and it surfaces as late; the typo sanity window is parked.
decisions.rationale: Per c-029: no plants source bounds the date, annex:6/functional/item:2 and section:non-compliance/para:2 require late notifications to be accepted, and file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2 needs a past date, so animals' lower bound (arrival.js:5) cannot be copied — a plants-source reason to diverge under standing ruling 5. The one sourced bound is reg 26(2)(a)'s 'date on which it first arrived', built as a max-only dateTextInRange (validators.js:269-271) inside POST from answers.arrivalStatus with the bounds helper beside the feature (docs/validation.md; skeleton date-fields). A potato already-arrived question is not a reg 24A(2) matter and NNS-UN-010 wants only proportionate questions — the c-002 hint line and the late flag cover the late-potato case. A sanity window's numbers have no source and are parked under standing ruling 1. Same shape as animals (dateText, kit.dateField, {day, month, year} storage), different policy, recorded on the obligation.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge's one-year-each-way sanity window with min/max on the picker — lost as at c-029: no source supplies the numbers, and a picker bound would display a rule the regulation does not impose.

decisions.resolution: Parked — no frontend increment. The notifier journey already collects what routing needs (commodityType and placeOfDestination), never asks the notifier which authority applies, shows no 'sent to X' copy, and keeps the confirmation's generic sentence that the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may carry out a spot check; routing, access parity and region derivation from the address are revisited when the plants backend has typed fields or an outbox.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(1) and reg:26(1) oblige the operator to notify 'the competent authority' without choosing one, so asking the notifier to pick or confirm an authority would invent an obligation they cannot reliably answer (NNS-UN-010). section:policy/para:7 ('Following receipt of a notification, the relevant competent authority (APHA, FC or Scottish Government) will undertake random spot checks at destination') and annex:6/functional/item:11 place routing and access on the system side after receipt; NNS-UN-029 and NNS-UN-030 are regulator needs met from the destination address and commodity type already collected. Nothing in this frontend can act on them: the mapper projects referenceNumber only, the backend NotificationDto has no typed fields, and outbox and GBN-AG publishing are out of scope on EUDPA-407 (skeleton persistence-and-mapper; sets/high-risk-plants/docs/limits.md) — new platform capability, which standing ruling 1 parks rather than builds or rejects. The engineering judge's buildability view decides build versus park. The confirmation's 'What happens next' sentence is kept because it is verbatim policy and collects nothing.
decisions.dissent: Policy judge: adopt, to record the frontend reading as built. Lost because there is no frontend increment to adopt — the frontend reading is already what the spec's pages do — and the behaviour itself is backend and internal-side work needing capability the plants backend lacks; the engineering judge's buildability view decides build versus park.

decisions.resolution: The Common Data contact is required and is satisfied by the one same-as-animals contactAddress pick: the picked address-book record carries name, address, telephone number and email address (the address-book API refuses a record without phone and email, and the plants client folds both into the address block), so 'Name of person making entry', 'Contact number', 'Contact address' and 'Contact email' are all collected by that single answer and nothing is asked twice. Consignment Number stays an optional free-text notifier reference on identification-numbers with the animals internalReferenceNumber input contract; its definition (issuer, format, potato applicability, whether it ever becomes mandatory) is parked as an open question, not built. Reading 'Name of person making entry' as the signed-in user is parked under standing ruling 2; in this pass the picked record's name is the nominated contact. The sub-park of 'Name of person making entry' as the signed-in user is decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2).
decisions.rationale: 'Common Data (if needed)' appears twice in the paper's own annexes (annex:2/common-data/item:1-5; annex:6/common-data/item:1-5 — verified at .sources/phnns-policy.txt lines 162-167 and 390-395) and nowhere in the draft SI (annex:5/reg:24A(2), reg:26(2)); the two Confluence pages and the mural carry no contact or consignment-number element at all, so the tier-2 sources add nothing. What makes the contact 'needed' is NNS-UN-040 ('nominated contact details for my consignment so that relevant parties can be informed about inspection activity') echoed by annex:6/functional/item:3 (sufficient detail to identify when spot checks are required); the user-needs extract's own implication is 'a per-consignment contact (distinct from the account holder)'. The four elements are one record: repos/trade-imports-address-book .../address/AddressRequest.java makes phone and email @NotBlank (20/254 max), repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend/src/server/app/services/address-book/client.js:60-63 maps them to address.telephoneNumber and address.emailAddress ('Contact details sit inside the address block'), stub/from-row.js:20-21 does the same, the animals party-picker copies the whole block inline (live-animals features/addresses/party-picker/selection.js:29-35, used by contact/controller.js:95) and the spec's address fieldGroup already lists telephoneNumber and emailAddress. One pick therefore meets Article 9(7) OCR 'strictly necessary' (section:legal-basis/para:1), NNS-UN-004 and annex:6/non-functional/item:10 'Minimise effort'. Consignment Number has no issuer, format or mandate in any source (extract.phnns-policy note: 'the paper does not say who issues it or whether it applies to potatoes, whose SI wording never uses the word consignment'; c-011), so under standing ruling 1 it cannot be required or validated — it stays the optional animals-shaped reference (live-animals origin.js internalReference, maxText 58, ^\w*$). Its label and hint are reconciler-invented, so the obligation is flagged provisional copy.

decisions.resolution: The animals shape wins outright. contactAddress (same-as-animals: flat radios over the organisation's address book, inline copy { addressId, name, address }) is the whole contact section, because the copied address block already carries telephoneNumber and emailAddress and the address-book API guarantees both are present. Delete the contactNumber and contactEmail obligations and the contact-details page; the contact task row completes on the pick alone and the opening run ends at consignment-contact-select (runStep 9 after c-034's renumbering) before landing on the hub. The plants Check your answers Contact card adds Telephone number and Email address rows read from the inline copy so the trader can see what will be submitted — animals' card shows name and address lines only, so this is a plants-only addition grounded in annex:6/common-data/item:2,4 and NNS-UN-007. Whether 'Name of person making entry' should be the signed-in user rather than the picked contact is parked under standing ruling 2 and recorded as an open-question behaviour.
decisions.rationale: The reconciler's second page rested on the gate question 'does the address-book record already carry phone/email?' and on the claim that the picker page has 'no telephone or email'. The code answers yes: AddressRequest.java makes phone and email @NotBlank; plants services/address-book/client.js:60-63 and stub/from-row.js:20-21 map them to address.telephoneNumber and address.emailAddress; animals answerFor stores { addressId, name, address: { ...chosen.address } } for the inline CONTACT_PARTY (selection.js:29-35; contact/controller.js:95) and the animals picker's address lines even list them (party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:20-21). A plants-only second page would ask twice for data the pick already holds and create two sources of truth for one contact — contrary to Article 9(7) OCR (section:legal-basis/para:1), NNS-UN-004 and NNS-UN-041, and a break from same-as-animals with no plants-source reason (standing ruling 5): annex:6/common-data/item:1-4 lists the four elements but never says they are typed, NNS-UN-040 names no elements, and the brief itself fixes the contact section as 'same-as-animals contactAddress; the animals shape is the address book picker'. Both readings are trivially buildable, so this is a consistency and minimum-data ruling, not a capability one. The one divergence the panel keeps is on Check your answers: the animals contact card renders name, address lines and country only (check-answers/view-model/rows/party-row.js:22-32), and since the plants notification will carry the record's telephone and email as its Common Data contact, NNS-UN-007 (confidence the information is complete and correct) needs them visible before submit — a plants-sourced reason. The contactEmail hint 'We will use this to tell the contact about any inspection' asserted a service behaviour no source gives and sat badly with checks-without-prior-notice (section:legal-basis/para:3/item:4); it goes with the page. A record edited or deleted in the INS address book after the pick does not reach the inline copy — same as animals, declared in the storage note. The 'signed-in user as the person making entry' reading touches sign-in models, which standing ruling 2 parks. Removing the page also breaks the e2e-contact-section anchor (after page:contact-details) and leaves stale mentions in opening-run, back-link-rules, section-captions, nfr-gdpr and c-011 — all swept below.

decisions.resolution: The SI wins on scope: the consignor is required for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees only and is never asked for potatoes — the potato list traces the crop through producer and crop identification numbers instead. The shape stays the variant-of-animals address-book picker with fieldGroupRef address and reference storage { addressId } resolved on read, gated same-frame on commodityType (activatedBy includes [plants-for-planting, wood-and-cut-trees], wipeOnExit true — the includesGate shape arrivalStatus already uses), so consignor-select is skipped by the opening run and its hub row hidden for potatoes. A typed name-and-address fallback for an EU consignor not yet in the address book is parked, not built: the trader adds it in the INS address book first, as animals traders do.
decisions.rationale: Reg 26(2)(f) 'the name and address of the consignor' sits in the plants-and-wood matters; reg 24A(2) lists eight potato matters and no consignor (verified at .sources/phnns-policy.txt lines 274-321). Annex 2 and Annex 6 repeat the split, and the policy team's two restatements agree (extract.confluence-requirements consignor under h4:All other goods/li:7 with the potato list carrying none; extract.mural consignorNameAndAddress under file:data-fields/region:Other goods/item:7 only). Four concordant sources are not an oversight — potatoes are traced through the producer identification number and crop identification number (reg 24A(2)(e)-(f)), which plants and wood do not have — so reading the omission as a drafting slip is a policy answer nobody has, which standing ruling 1 parks and standing ruling 4 (the SI is the authority on WHAT is collected) forbids the panel to overrule; Article 9(7) OCR 'strictly necessary' (section:legal-basis/para:1) and NNS-UN-004/NNS-UN-010 point the same way. The gate is buildable today: activatedBy { obligation: commodityType, includes: [...] } with wipeOnExit is the same-frame shape the spec already uses on arrivalStatus (skeleton helper vocabulary: includesGate on a top-level scalar), the derived page gate hides consignor-select and the row status rules mark the row NA (hub-task-list-and-row-status). The address book is the party source the engine has: skeleton ambiguity (e) is settled by the adopted address-book-picker behaviour, animals stores { addressId } resolved on read (live-animals parties.js:12; plants services/address-book/index.js all/party), and writes belong to the INS frontend. A typed fallback is an address-form page plus a second storage shape for one party that no plants source asks for (the SI says 'name and address', not 'typed'); the 'EU consignor unlikely to be in the book' worry is an operating assumption, so it is parked with one note for the revisit: the INS address book demands a phone and email that reg 26(2)(f) does not (AddressRequest.java) — a friction animals already lives with.

decisions.resolution: Keep the animals id, page, widget, validation, label, hint and Welsh label and hint verbatim; change only the error sentence to 'Select the country where the consignment originates from' — one noun swapped in the animals sentence — and drop the copied Welsh error rather than ship one that names an animal (the build's copy.cy.js carries a machine-draft leaf under the welsh-copy-seam banner so the parity tripwire still passes; no Welsh is invented in the spec). Because one copy string now differs, tag the obligation variant-of-animals — its divergence being this error sentence and the per-category origin narrowing ruled at c-022 — and flag the error sentence provisional copy.
decisions.rationale: The SI names the subject of the element as the goods, not an animal: 'the country from which the plants or wood originate' (annex:5/reg:26(2)(e)) and 'the country from which the potatoes originate' (annex:5/reg:24A(2)(ab)), restated at h4:All other goods/li:5 and h4:Potatoes (seed and ware)/li:3. The animals error copy 'Select the country where the animal originates from' (repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend .../features/origin/copy/copy.en.js:24; live-animals origin.js:12) would be a false statement on a plants page, and the live-animals extract's own note lists animals-specific copy as not to be copied verbatim — that is the plants-source reason to diverge that standing ruling 5 requires. The brief defines same-as-animals as same copy and validation, so an obligation with one changed string (and, under c-022, added validation) is honestly a variant; the tag costs nothing (the copy-parity tripwire compares plants en/cy pairs, not plants against animals — skeleton tripwire-copy-parity). Among the three candidate sentences the chair takes the engine judge's 'the consignment': it is the smallest possible departure from the animals sentence (the epic's 'consistent, not shared' principle prefers the minimum justified change), 'the consignment' is the SI's own noun for the goods in reg 26(2)(a)-(d) and is already the plants copy's word on the arrival-status and contact pages, it is commodity-neutral so one string serves potatoes, plants and wood with no per-type copy switch (one obligation per c-015), and it still says what to do in plain English. errorCopyCy is removed because the brief says do not invent Welsh; the cy leaf must exist for copy-parity, so it is machine-drafted at build under the existing MACHINE-DRAFT banner (skeleton welsh-copy-seam) and flagged provisional with the English.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge preferred 'Select the country of origin' (echoes the label, terse) and the policy judge preferred 'Select the country the plants, wood or potatoes originate from' (names the SI subjects). Both lost to the engine judge's wording: the label-echo drops the animals sentence shape entirely when a one-noun swap keeps it (standing ruling 5 favours the smallest justified divergence), and the three-commodity list names goods the trader is not importing and is longer with no source requiring the enumeration. All three agreed on everything else (verbatim label/hint/Welsh, no invented Welsh error, variant-of-animals tag).

decisions.resolution: Keep the declaration page and its machinery exactly as animals has them — the single checkbox, its confirmation sentence in English and Welsh, the error copy, the date line, Continue, the flow-only key and submit gate. Replace the five animals statements wholesale: none survives. The first pass carries three short plants statements grounded in the policy paper — (1) this submission is the written notification to the competent authority under the Plant Health National Notification Scheme; (2) the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may spot-check the consignment without prior notice at its place of destination or where it is currently held; (3) failing to notify, notifying late or giving incorrect details may be treated as a non-compliance — flagged provisional copy for policy and content-design sign-off, with no Welsh invented. The third-party / agent-authority clauses are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2, not written, and every spec line saying the plants declaration 'carries the third-party clause' is corrected. The sub-park of the third-party and agent-authority clauses is decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2).
decisions.rationale: No plants source prescribes declaration wording: the SI requires only 'written notification to the competent authority' by the professional operator (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)); the paper, both Confluence pages and the mural are silent; the prototype has a declaration checkbox and submit with no statements (extract.prototype declaration route). The engine already supports the shape (skeleton flow-only-keys-declaration; adopted declaration-and-submit-gate), so the checkbox, sentence and semantics are a same-as-animals first-pass build. The truth-and-accuracy checkbox is grounded — 'Incorrect notification details' is a named non-compliance (section:non-compliance/para:2/item:2) and NNS-UN-007 wants confidence the notification is complete and correct — so the animals sentence stands verbatim. Each animals statement (repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend .../features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js) fails a plants source: 'cleared border control checks' contradicts the premise that border controls are removed (section:policy/para:1-2; customs-no-sps-hold-or-matching); 'payments for border control checks' contradicts the no-fees decision (section:fees-and-charges/para:1; no-fees-no-payment-step); 'quarantine or isolation of the animals' is on the live-animals extract's LIVE-ANIMALS-SPECIFIC COPY list; 're-dispatch', 'destruction and disposal' and 'contact for the authorities and located in the UK' have no plants source. The two clauses on acting for a third party assert a delegation model that standing ruling 2 puts out of this phase — they are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf (NNS-UN-039) — and the GDS judge's 'I am the professional operator ... or I am authorised to make this notification on their behalf' would also decide c-038 (who notifies) by the back door. The three replacement statements restate facts the paper already asserts rather than imposing new undertakings: written-notification-attributable (reg 24A(1)/26(1)); random spot checks at destination by APHA, FC or Scottish Government (section:policy/para:7) without prior notice (section:legal-basis/para:3/item:4; checks-without-prior-notice-no-booking-step), with 'where it is currently held' covering the already-arrived branch (reg 26(2)(b)); and the paper's three non-compliance examples in full (section:non-compliance/para:2 — failure to notify, incorrect details, late) rather than late alone (late-accepted-not-rejected). They are provisional copy pending policy sign-off; Welsh is not invented (brief).
decisions.dissent: GDS judge wanted a first statement 'I am the professional operator bringing this consignment into England, or I am authorised to make this notification on their behalf', treating the authority clause as copy rather than a feature. Lost under standing ruling 2: a declaration statement is a legal assertion the notifier signs, so asserting authority to act for another is delegation of authority — out of this phase — and 'I am the professional operator' pre-empts c-038. The engine judge's non-compliance statement covered late notification only; the policy judge's wider wording (failure to notify, late, incorrect details — all three paper examples) was preferred. The policy judge's spot-check statement was widened with the engine judge's already-arrived branch ('or where it is currently held', reg 26(2)(b)).

decisions.resolution: Seed potatoes are potatoes: commodityType = potatoes, the per-line category offers seed-potatoes and ware-potatoes, and a seed-potato line takes the reg 24A matters (variety, quantity, intended use, producer and crop ids, time of arrival, place of landing) and the two-day pre-arrival window. The mural list-image's placement of seed potatoes under Plants for planting is not followed and 'Seed potatoes' is never a genus value.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(1)(a) names seed potatoes as the first class of potatoes and reg 24A(1)(b) defines ware as 'potatoes, other than seed potatoes', so seed potatoes carry the reg 24A(2) matters and the 'at least two days before' timing. Annex 1 lists 'Seed potatoes' as its own item beside 'Ware potatoes', not under plants for planting; the mural data-fields board (file:data-fields/region:Potatoes (ware and seed)) and the Confluence page (h4:Potatoes (seed and ware)) agree. Only mural list-image row 16 dissents and its own note (seed-potatoes-listed-under-plants-for-planting) says the board does not resolve it; standing ruling 4 puts the policy paper first. The two category values are needed because the origin scope differs (seed: any part of the Common SPS Area bar the UK, Channel Islands and Isle of Man; ware: Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain). The spec already carries this on commodityType.input.values, category.input.valuesByCommodityType.potatoes, potatoVariety/potatoIntendedUse gated on the two potato categories, arrivalTime gated on commodityType = potatoes, and genus.input.valuesNote ('seed potatoes are not a genus'). All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: The SI wording wins: the category value is conifer-wood-with-bark, labelled 'Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer'. The mural table's 'with mark' is a transcription typo and carries no meaning.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i) reads 'conifer wood with bark and isolated bark of conifer from a member State, excluding preservative-treated wood'. The mural extract's own transcription-drift note records that the embedded OFFSEN image (file:list-image/row:18) reads 'bark' and only the Mural-native re-typed table (file:list-table/row:18) reads 'mark'; both mural forms truncate the SI item anyway. Tier one over tier two under standing ruling 4. The spec's category.input.valueLabels already carries the SI reading; the label stays provisional for the copy pass and needs Welsh before release (nfr-english-and-welsh). All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: The four wood caveats are scope conditions, not data elements: they become the five wood category values (with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in the value labels) and guidance copy; the only extra wood data collected is the two SI matters, size of tree and phytosanitary treatments, gated same-frame on category. No question is asked about preservative treatment, bark condition or the 3-metre threshold. The preservative exclusion moves from the treatments hint to a hint on the category question shown for wood notifications, worded with its cut-coniferous-trees exception.
decisions.rationale: The SI separates scope from matters: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i)-(iv) says who must notify (bark, origin, preservative exclusion, height, form) and reg 26(2)(h)-(i) are the only wood matters. Article 9(7) OCR limits notification data to what is 'strictly necessary' (section:legal-basis/para:1), so a preservative or height question would collect a datum the SI does not list; a consignment outside reg 26(1)(b) attracts no duty. The mural author offers the caveats 'in case you need this level of detail' (file:data-fields/region:Wood/preamble, note wood-caveats-are-scope-detail) and the Confluence extractor flagged the heading as ambiguous rather than as a data claim. Engine: category is a within-member gate so allowListed(category, values, null) scopes sizeOfTree and phytosanitaryTreatments per line with no modelGap (add-a-collection.md section 2). Two corrections to the spec as drafted. First, the scope condition must be visible at the moment of choosing (NNS-UN-013 wood importer, NNS-UN-010 proportionate), not only in the treatments hint the trader sees after committing to a wood category. Second, the current treatments hint 'Preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified' is gated on all five wood categories including cut-coniferous-trees, yet reg 26(1)(b)(iii) carries no preservative exclusion, so on a cut-trees line that sentence is wrong; a single wood-level hint on the category question with the exception stated says it once and correctly. Per-option hints repeating the four-country and 3-metre conditions are not added because the value labels already carry them.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge wanted per-option hints on all five wood values ('Does not include preservative-treated wood' on four of them, plus the four-country and 3-metre conditions restated) — lost because the value labels already carry the origin and height conditions and one wood-level hint with the cut-trees exception states the preservative rule once without contradicting item (iii). Policy judge proposed no spec change at all — lost on the cut-trees point: the existing treatments hint is wrong for a cut-coniferous-trees line.

decisions.resolution: '(for plants for planting)' qualifies species only. Genus is asked for plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, hardwood-round-surface and hardwood-chips lines; species only for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting; the three conifer lines (conifer-wood-with-bark, conifer-wood-without-bark, cut-coniferous-trees) ask neither in the first pass. The literal reading that reg 26(2)(c) also wants a genus for conifer wood is recorded on the obligation as a parked policy check, not built.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(c) reads 'the category (e.g. plants for planting or cut wood), genus, species (for plants for planting) and commodity code'; the bracket sits immediately after species, and where the SI qualifies a whole matter it leads with 'in the case of' (reg 26(2)(g)-(i)), so species is plants-for-planting only. Genus for hardwood lines is a statutorily listed value (reg 26(1)(b)(iv) 'wood of Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus') and is offered. For conifer wood the scope items say only 'conifer' and no source supplies a conifer genus list, so a conifer genus control cannot be populated today (standing ruling 1); a free-text genus with no list and no validation runs against Annex 6 'Standardise information' and 'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8-9) and is impractical for isolated bark and mixed chips. The policy judge's claim that Annex 3 reaches for conifer genus does not survive reading it: Annex 3's Wood products section groups pests under 'Cut coniferous trees>3m', 'Conifer wood with bark and all isolated conifer bark' and 'Conifer wood without bark' (Ips, Bursaphelenchus, Fusarium by bark condition and form), and names a genus only for hardwood ('Wood of ash', 'Wood of Castanea', 'Wood of Platanus') — which is exactly the split the spec makes. Confluence (h4:All other goods/li:3 with its qualifier note) and the mural (file:data-fields/region:Other goods/item:3) carry the same sentence and cannot tip it. The spec's genus.activatedBy.includes and species.activatedBy.includes already encode this; the note makes the omission deliberate and revisitable when policy answers.
decisions.dissent: Policy judge: genus is unqualified in reg 26(2)(c) and applies to every plants or wood line, so conifer lines should ask genus as required free text (requiredMaxText 58) until a list exists — lost because no source gives a conifer genus list (standing ruling 1), Annex 3 on inspection groups conifer wood by bark and form rather than genus so the statute does not reach for it, and an unvalidated free-text genus contradicts Annex 6 items 8-9; the reading is preserved as a parked policy check.

decisions.resolution: The hardwood genus constraint is Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. Juglans and Pterocarya are not offered anywhere in the service; the mural and Confluence lists that still carry them (and the mural spelling 'Juglens') are superseded by the SI footnotes.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(iv) lists 'wood of Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus' and footnotes 2 and 3 (policy extract juglans-pterocarya-removed-from-scope, provenance footnote:2, alsoStatedAt footnote:3) say Juglans and Pterocarya 'were included in the original scope but have now been removed as they are no longer considered to be hosts of Agrilus planipennis'. The mural (file:list-image/row:22, 'Juglens') and the Confluence caveats (h4:Additional caveats for wood products/li:4) predate that removal and are tier two under standing ruling 4. Offering an out-of-scope genus would invite notifications the scheme does not require (NNS-UN-010). The spec's genus.input.valuesByCategory already reads Castanea, Fraxinus, Platanus for both hardwood categories; the list lives in the set-owned commodities service checked by whitelists.test.js (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:2, annex:1 closing paragraph), so a future reinstatement is a data change. All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: A notification carries one or many commodity lines: commodityLines is a collection with minEntries 1 (error 'Add at least one commodity'), built as the two-page batch (list page plus Commodity details entry sub-page) as a variant of animals' commodityLines without its catalogue search. All lines share the one commodityType chosen first; a consignment mixing potatoes with plants or wood is two notifications. Bulk upload of many notifications is a separate matter already parked under c-040.
decisions.rationale: The SI's singular 'the consignment' (annex:5/reg:26(2)(c)-(d), reg:24A(2)(d)) describes the movement, not a cap on its contents: a consignment of two genera or several potato varieties can only meet 'genus, species ... commodity code' and 'their variety and quantity' by reporting each. NNS-UN-005 ('large shipments efficiently ... high volumes of consignments') and NNS-UN-006 ('detailed and flexible product information') push toward many lines; the mural's 59k notifications a year (file:blueprint/left header card) is volume, not lines. The reg 24A / reg 26 split (different matters, different windows) justifies one commodityType per notification (one-notification-per-commodity-type, adopted). Engine: collections are first-class (skeleton collections-engine-api; add-a-collection.md section 1 requires.minEntries) and collections-two-page-batch is adopted; animals' commodityLines is the consistency anchor (standing ruling 5) with the divergence recorded on the obligation. The spec already says all of this. All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: Wipe wins: wipeOnExit = true stays on every gated plants obligation and no answer is retained out of scope. A change of commodityType after lines exist is handled in the commodity-type page's POST, not on the list page's load: the page warns before the change when lines exist, the POST commits the type and then drops the lines whose category is not in the new type's set via reconcileEntriesAt, and redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> where a notification banner names what was removed; the list page suppresses its zero-lines redirect for that load and never writes on GET.
decisions.rationale: No plants source asks for retention: NNS-UN-041 is about reusing a previous consignment (reuse-previous-consignment, parked) and NNS-UN-006's 'flexible' is coloured red, meaning unstated. Policy points to wipe: Annex 6 'Standardise information' and 'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8-9), Article 9(7) strictly-necessary (section:legal-basis/para:1), and 'Incorrect notification details' as a named non-compliance (section:non-compliance list) — a wood notification still carrying a potato variety is exactly that. The engine's Yes-No-Yes rule is the default (docs/scope-and-wipe.md: 'when a controlling answer makes a value leave scope, the value is deleted. Returning to the earlier branch does not restore stale data') and animals' only retain is regionOfOriginCode, so wipe also keeps consistency under standing ruling 5. For the lines, category is always in scope on the line and 'a value-list mismatch is not a scope condition' (skeleton helper-selection-rule), so the model cannot drop them; but reconcileEntriesAt exists (engine/write/entries/reconcile.js, exported from engine/index.js) and keys existing entries, keeps those still present and drops the rest with wipe semantics, and animals reconciles commodityLines by lineKey on the save that changes the selection (live-animals extract, commodities search page). The reconciler's provisional pick — reconcile on the list page's load — fails twice: add-a-collection.md forbids a GET triggering a delete ('no GET can trigger a delete'), and a trader who changes type from a CYA Change link is returned to CYA by kit.exitTarget (skeleton change context) without visiting the list, leaving stale lines counted complete by the hub, CYA and submit. Doing it in the POST that changes the controlling answer closes the hole at the moment it opens. The count travels on the redirect query string because that is the engine's own post-redirect convention (shared/kit.js:177 sets ?staleAction=1); the engine judge's 'no yar' claim is wrong (yar backs the session cache) but the precedent stands. Because the nine categories partition by type, kept is empty whenever the type really changes, which is why the warning text before the change is worth its one line. One hole the judges missed: the commodities list page redirects to the entry sub-page whenever it has zero lines (page shape, copied from animals emptyRedirect inverted), so a ?removed load must render rather than redirect or the banner is never seen. Three typed collections (three groups, duplicated quantity/genus/commodityCode/use, three CYA cards) and retain-and-flag (an unsubmittable notification the trader cannot fix from CYA) are not built.

decisions.resolution: The genus list for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting lines is the fifteen entries of reg 26(1)(a) with the SI's spelling and bracketed English names; the four species-level entries are offered as they stand; 'Seed potatoes' is not a genus; hardwood lines get the same control rendered with Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. The list is set-owned reference data, not a hard-coded enum, and the details page offers only the entries allowed for the line's category — never fifteen with twelve rejected.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(a)(i)-(xv) is the statutory list and tier one ('Polygala myrtifolia (myrtle-leaf milkwort)', 'Salvia rosmarinus (rosemary)'); Annex 1 holds the same fifteen regrouped as ten plus five Xylella shrub hosts, so there is no drift inside the policy paper. The mural's sixteenth row is seed potatoes, ruled a potato under c-004, and its 'Salvia Rosmarinus' and 'myrtle leaved milkwort' are tier-two transcription variants (file:list-image/rows:1-16). The Confluence page gives no list. Annex 6 wants 'easy maintenance of ... Genus & species in scope' (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:2) and Annex 1's closing paragraph says the list 'will be dynamic', which the set-owned commodities service and whitelists.test.js satisfy (set-owned-commodities-service, restore-whitelists-test). The bracketed common names keep the control plain English for a trader who knows 'oak' not 'Quercus'. Because commodity-details is server-rendered on POST after category is chosen (page shape), the option list itself can be the per-category list; the spec's 'narrowed by page-side validation' alone reads as fifteen rendered and twelve rejected, which the GOV.UK error pattern discourages, so the note is tightened.

decisions.resolution: commodityType has three values (potatoes / plants-for-planting / wood-and-cut-trees) and the per-line category has nine (seed-potatoes, ware-potatoes, plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, conifer-wood-with-bark, conifer-wood-without-bark, cut-coniferous-trees, hardwood-round-surface, hardwood-chips); the commodity-details page offers only the categories of the chosen type and POST rejects any other. The mural's five coarse labels are not a value list.
decisions.rationale: The three types are the SI's own partition — reg 24A (potatoes), reg 26(1)(a) (plants for planting), reg 26(1)(b) (wood and cut trees) — with different matters and timing windows, matching the mural's data-fields regions and Annex 1's headings. The SI only exemplifies category ('e.g. plants for planting or cut wood', annex:5/reg:26(2)(c)), so the value list is derived from the scope items themselves: reg 24A(1)(a)/(b), reg 26(1)(a) split by c-019, reg 26(1)(b)(i), (ii), (iii), (iv)(aa), (iv)(bb); every value is traceable to a statutory item and each carries distinct scope conditions and gated matters. Collapsing to the mural's Plants for planting / Ware potatoes / Bark / Wood / Cut Trees (file:list-image/column:1) would lose the bark-by-origin and round-surface/chips distinctions the SI needs (c-037) and the potato split (c-004). Two questions rather than one is right under one-thing-per-page: the type page is three radios that decide the journey, the category page two to five radios per line. Engine: category sits on the line so every per-line gate is same-frame allowListed with no modelGap; the type filter is controller validation from the set-owned service. The spec already says this. All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: Keep 'trees for planting' as a per-line category value beside 'plants for planting' so the notifier declares that the plants are trees and sizeOfTree gates same-frame on category in [trees-for-planting, cut-coniferous-trees]. Both options get a neutral hint that lets the trader self-classify without policy knowledge; the genus list is not narrowed for trees for planting. Which plants-for-planting lines legally count as trees is a parked policy question, and the genus-derived alternative is not built.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(h) requires 'in the case of cut trees or trees for planting, the size of the tree' but reg 26(1) defines no 'trees for planting' class: plants for planting are scoped by genus and only cut coniferous trees by height (reg 26(1)(b)(iii)). Annex 1's split is the only hint and it is never labelled 'trees' — Olea europaea sits in the first group while Annex 3 lists it as a Xylella host, and Prunus is grown as a shrub — so reading the first group as a legal tree list would invent a classification. The notifier already has to know whether the plants are trees to know whether the SI requires size, so asking them to say so makes the statutory condition answerable without inventing an obligation; asking size of every plants-for-planting line would over-collect against Article 9(7) and NNS-UN-010. Engine: 'genus in tree genera OR category = cut-coniferous-trees' is two conditions on one obligation, which the helper vocabulary does not offer (skeleton helper-selection-rule; a gate reads one gate value), and the only expressible genus-driven form is two size obligations, splitting one statutory matter into two CYA rows against c-015; under standing ruling 1 the category value is what is built now. The residual design risk is a trader not knowing whether their Quercus whips are 'trees', so the two options carry hints; the copy is invented and provisional.
decisions.dissent: Policy judge wanted the trees-for-planting hint to name Annex 1's first-group genera as the trees ('sweet chestnut, cedar, ash, olive, spruce, pine, plane, plum or cherry, oak or elm') — lost because Annex 1 never labels that group 'trees', Olea and Prunus sit in it awkwardly, and naming them would put a policy classification nobody made into notifier-facing copy; the neutral self-classification hint is used instead. Engine judge proposed no hint at all — lost because a self-classification radio needs a hint the trader can act on (NNS-UN-011, NNS-UN-004).

decisions.resolution: Genus is a controlled list from the set-owned commodities service; species is required free text (requiredMaxText 58, no format check) on plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting lines until a species catalogue exists; the four species-level scope entries (Olea europaea, Nerium oleander, Polygala myrtifolia, Salvia rosmarinus) are offered as genus values exactly as the SI spells them.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(2)(c) requires 'species (for plants for planting)' and gives no list; the statutory scope is genus-level except for those four entries (reg 26(1)(a)(vi), (vii), (xi), (xiv)). Annex 6's 'easy maintenance of ... Genus & species in scope' (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:2) describes a future catalogue no source supplies, so a coded species control would be invented (standing ruling 1); 'Standardise information' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8) is met at genus level where a list exists. NNS-UN-006's 'flexible' free text and NNS-UN-016/017's coded values are both honoured by the split, and the c-011 pattern (free text, 58 characters mirroring animals text inputs) keeps the input consistent. When a catalogue arrives the widget becomes an autocomplete over the service — a data-plus-widget change, not a model change. The spec's species obligation and genus.input.values already say this. All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: The SI's two items win: conifer-wood-with-bark ('Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer', any member State) and conifer-wood-without-bark ('Conifer wood without bark', Italy, France, Portugal and Spain only), with the four-country origin constraint on the second value alone. The Confluence and mural rephrasing is not modelled as a third value.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i) 'conifer wood with bark and isolated bark of conifer from a member State' and (ii) 'conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain'. The tier-two restatement 'with or without bark ... from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain' (h4:Additional caveats for wood products/li:2; file:data-fields/region:Wood/bullet:2) folds with-bark wood from those four countries into (ii), which (i) already covers from any member State — the same practical scope, but its wording would put an origin constraint on with-bark wood that the SI does not impose; standing ruling 4 takes the SI. Annex 3 confirms the split is deliberate (Bursaphelenchus xylophilus 'from France, Portugal, Spain' listed under 'Conifer wood without bark'). Two values keep the origin narrowing a per-category allow-list (countryOfOrigin.input.valueConstraints conifer-wood-without-bark = [IT, FR, PT, ES]) and the category label names the four countries so the trader can self-select before the origin page (commodity precedes origin, c-022). Whether an out-of-scope origin is rejected or accepted is origin-value-list-by-commodity, not on this docket. All three judges agree.

decisions.resolution: Build it in the first pass exactly as ruled in c-013: the commodity-type POST, after committing a changed commodityType, reconciles commodityLines with reconcileEntriesAt (keep lines whose category is in the new type's set, drop the rest with wipe semantics), the page warns before when lines exist, and it redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> where a notification banner reports the removal and the zero-lines redirect is suppressed for that load. The on-load reconcile, three typed collections and retain-and-flag alternatives are not built; a model-owned projection helper is recorded as a candidate extension.
decisions.rationale: The engine already exposes reconcileEntriesAt with wipe semantics (engine/write/entries/reconcile.js keeps entries still present by key and drops the rest; skeleton collections-engine-api) and animals reconciles by key on the save that changes the controlling selection (live-animals commodities search page), so the increment is one branch in the commodity-type POST, one banner on the list page, and tests in controller.test.js — cheap and consistent under standing ruling 5. The model cannot own it because a value-list mismatch is not a scope condition (skeleton helper-selection-rule) and per-instance scope wipes fields, not instances (skeleton scope-and-wipe). Reconciling on list-page load would write on GET, which add-a-collection.md forbids for deletes, or leave a wood notification carrying a seed-potato line that the hub, CYA and submit count complete until the page is revisited — a hole a CYA Change link on commodity-type opens directly. Three typed collections would triple the collection pages and duplicate quantity against NNS-UN-004 and the one-obligation-per-concept reading in c-015; retain-and-flag leaves an unsubmittable notification. The e2e-commodity-section extra already names 'changing commodity type drops incompatible lines'.

decisions.resolution: Build the guidance reading: the five wood category values encode the SI items with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in their labels, and the preservative exclusion is a hint on the category question for wood notifications with its cut-coniferous-trees exception (the c-007 edit); no pre-scope question and no 'you do not need to notify' page. Fuller scope text belongs with guidance-before-you-start, outside the journey pages. Explicit scope questions that end the journey are parked pending a policy answer, not built.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i)-(iv) states every caveat as a condition on who must notify, not a matter under reg 26(2); Article 9(7) OCR confines the notification to what is strictly necessary (section:legal-basis/para:1), so a preservative or height question whose answer is never a matter would collect data from people with no duty. The mural author offers the caveats 'in case you need this level of detail' (file:data-fields/region:Wood/preamble) and NNS-UN-013 (wood importer wants to understand what is required) is met by making the scope visible on the category options at the moment of choosing. The preservative exclusion attaches to items (i), (ii) and (iv) but not (iii), and the 3-metre threshold only to (iii); the labels and the wood hint keep those attachments. No source asks for an end-of-journey 'not notifiable' page or screening questions, so under standing ruling 1 they are parked inside the detail. Engine: radios with hints are govuk-toolbox; the gates are same-frame allowListed on category; nothing needs a model change.

decisions.resolution: Build it: the seed/ware split is the per-line category; the origin narrowing is validation owned by origin-value-list-by-commodity (its reject-or-accept question stays open there); the ware-potato origin scope and the Balearic Islands exclusion are one govukInsetText on the origin page, rendered page-side only when a ware-potatoes line exists, so countryOfOrigin's label, hint and widget stay verbatim animals (the obligation is tagged variant-of-animals for its validation and error sentence — c-022, c-027). 'Suspected of having been grown' is not asked; a Spain region option and the mural's off-board footnote are parked.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(1)(a)-(b) sets the potato scope by category and origin and reg 24A(3) defines 'Spain' as excluding the Balearic Islands; these are conditions on the duty, not matters under reg 24A(2), whose only origin datum is 'the country from which the potatoes originate' (reg 24A(2)(ab)). Under Article 9(7) (section:legal-basis/para:1) they are carried as copy, and 'grown or suspected of having been grown' widens who must notify without creating anything to declare. The mural's 'Spain & Poland' (file:list-image/row:17) and its use cases are tier two; the SI's four countries win (c-021). The inset says only what the country list cannot express — the four-country scope and the Balearic exclusion — and is shown only when a ware-potatoes line exists (NNS-UN-011, NNS-UN-004); the seed-potato scope is the country list itself, and the narrowing's enforcement is origin-value-list-by-commodity's question. Rendering it page-side rather than on the obligation keeps countryOfOrigin's label, hint and widget verbatim animals (standing ruling 5; its validation and error sentence diverge under c-022 and c-027), with reg 24A(3) as the plants-sourced reason for the one plants-only line of copy. No source supplies a Spanish region list and the plants origin page dropped animals' region code, so a Balearic option is parked (standing ruling 1). The origin page notes and c-021 cite a behaviour id 'spain-excludes-balearic-islands' that does not exist in behaviours[]; the reference is repointed to this behaviour.
decisions.dissent: Engine judge wanted the Balearic sentence as a conditional hint on the countryOfOrigin obligation beside the animals hint — lost because the obligation's hint is verbatim animals and a page-side inset delivers the same copy without diverging (standing ruling 5). Policy judge wanted two sentences shown on every potato notification (seed and ware scope) — lost because the seed-potato sentence restates the country list and the narrowing is validation under origin-value-list-by-commodity, so only the ware sentence adds information the list cannot carry.

decisions.resolution: Proceed on the two Confluence pages exactly as extracted (requirements v5 2026-07-02, user needs v11 2026-06-30). The SharePoint workbook 'EU Reset Delivery Programme_Requirements Template.xlsx' is not a source in this run, is not chased, and nothing in the spec waits on it; if it is ever read, each difference from the pages becomes a new conflict against the policy paper, which still wins.
decisions.rationale: Both extracts record the workbook as a pointer nobody could open: extract.confluence-requirements notes 'POINTER, not fetched' for the h2 Requirements catalogue panel (sourcedoc 3ABC6624) and extract.confluence-user-needs records the para:sharepoint-link / panel:note ('User needs will be transferred to the table below at the conclusion of the NNS exploration phase'). Standing ruling 1 parks anything that needs a source nobody could read rather than blocking on it. Standing ruling 4 puts phnns-policy above the Confluence tier, and the statutory list in annex:5/reg:24A(2) and reg:26(2) is complete on its own, so a lagging workbook cannot change WHAT is collected, only how the policy team restates it. The 'True at time of publishing' line (h1:Notification Data Requirements/info) is a volatility note, not a disagreement, and every Confluence-derived obligation already carries its page provenance. Widening the source list is a later-phase decision; the reconciler's provisional pick stands and the spec already reflects it.

decisions.resolution: The SI wins: the notifier is the professional operator bringing the goods into England, and in this service that is the signed-in Defra ID organisation. The journey collects no importer, agent or notifier party; the consignor (reg 26(2)(f)) is the only party obligation. The declaration carries no third-party, standing, authority or agent sentence — both animals third-party statements are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2 (c-028) — and its statement bullets are the three plants statements ruled at c-028. Agent identification, authorisation and linking stay parked under agent-acting-on-behalf. || Detail note (specChange from c-028): the provisional pick's sentence 'the declaration copy carries the third-party clause' in this conflict's detail is superseded by c-028 — the clause is parked with agent-acting-on-behalf, not carried; this ruling does not reinstate it.
decisions.rationale: annex:5/reg:24A(1) and reg:26(1) place the duty on 'A professional operator who is bringing ... into England' (phnns-policy.txt:274, 289); neither list of matters asks for the notifier's own details and reg 26(2)(f) names only 'the name and address of the consignor' (phnns-policy.txt:321). 'Importers will be required to complete a PHNSS notification' (section:policy/para:6, phnns-policy.txt:16) is the policy team's plain-English restatement and ranks below the SI (standing ruling 4). NNS-UN-039 is malformed ('so that I can so that I can') and the extractor records that the page 'does not say how an agent is identified, authorised or linked to the importer' (extract.confluence-user-needs:730); the mural's 'Importer, agent' actor (file:blueprint/Setup actions, Import notification) is a persona, not a data element. Standing ruling 2 puts agents, delegation and 'who is the notifier' out of this phase. Buildable as-is: the engine scopes every journey to the session organisation (repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend/src/server/app/engine/journey.js:107-124, organisationIdOf) and animals collects no separate notifier either. Neither of animals' two third-party statements (extract.live-animals:1931) survives: a declaration statement is a legal assertion the notifier signs, so 'I can legally act on behalf of a third party' asserts a delegation of authority the phase does not model (standing ruling 2, c-028), and 'I am authorised as being accountable for these things ...' also depends on the animals accountability list (border-control payments, quarantine, destruction) that c-028 replaces; consistency (standing ruling 5) yields to the standing ruling.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge: proposed retaining both animals third-party statements and setting provisionalCopy=true on the declaration page. Lost on the statements: both are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2 (c-028) — a declaration statement is a legal assertion the notifier signs — and 'I am authorised as being accountable for these things' also depends on the animals accountability list that c-028 replaces. On the flag: provisionalCopy: true is already set on the declaration page under c-028 because its statement bullets are not verbatim animals; titleCy stays because the title is.

decisions.resolution: Defra ID sign-in (real mode /auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-in-oidc, /auth/organisation; stub mode /auth/stub-sign-in) is the only precondition to notifying built in this run. No plant-operator registration page, registration check before the dashboard or onboarding step; the dashboard is reachable by any authenticated organisation. Plant-operator registration stays parked under plant-operator-registration.
decisions.rationale: NNS-UN-038 ('register myself as a plant operator so that I can notify authorities') is one of two orange-highlighted rows with no legend — the extractor says 'could mean new, contested, or out of scope. Treat both as unconfirmed' (extract.confluence-user-needs:722). The mural's 'Register for new [GB product] — Importer, agent' (file:blueprint/region:Setup actions; extract.mural:298, 715) has the product in placeholder brackets. The policy paper's only access requirement is 'System is secure (userid & password to access for internal users)' (annex:6/non-functional/item:4, phnns-policy.txt:364) — silent on external notifiers — and the SI imposes a duty to notify, not to register (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)). Standing ruling 2 parks plant-operator registration. The engine already enforces sign-in on every route (skeleton authSignIn, servedToday yes, src/server/auth/index.js:8-15; 'auth is still enforced' even in STUB_MODE) and animals has no registration step, so sign-in-only is both the buildable reading (standing ruling 1) and the same-as-animals shape (standing ruling 5). The adopted behaviour stub-mode-and-sign-in already says 'Sign-in is the only precondition to notifying built in this run (c-039)'.

decisions.resolution: The many-lines reading of NNS-UN-005 is met by the commodityLines collection: one notification, one or many lines, at least one, no maximum (c-012). Bulk upload of many notifications at once, import from existing documents and reuse of a previous consignment are not built and each stays its own parked behaviour; no file page, upload route or format enters the start section, and nothing in the form is shaped around a future file route. Annex 6's bulk-upload line is recorded as met later, not now.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/functional/item:6 'Provide the option to bulk upload (external) to or download data (internal) from the system' (phnns-policy.txt:353) names no format, schema or unit of upload; the extractor records NNS-UN-005 as 'ambiguous whether this means one notification with many lines, many notifications at once (bulk upload), or both' (extract.confluence-user-needs:742). Standing ruling 3 puts bulk upload out of phase. The SI describes one consignment's category/genus/species/commodity code/quantity (annex:5/reg:26(2)(c)-(d), reg:24A(2)(d)), and a mixed consignment needs several lines — the collection describes it lawfully without a second entry route. The many-lines reading is buildable now: collections-two-page-batch is adopted over the engine's collection primitives (skeleton collections-engine-api) mirroring animals' commodities shape, and the commodityLines obligation already carries minEntries 1, 'no maximum given by any source', provenance NNS-UN-005 and mandateRaw citing c-012. Nothing in the spec needs to move.

decisions.resolution: Not built in this phase. No file, template or upload page appears in the spec. Recorded as a later alternative entry route in the start section that must produce the same canonical fulfilment and pass the same validation as the form, once policy supplies the format, scope and unit of upload.
decisions.rationale: Standing ruling 3 (bulk upload is OUT). Sources: annex:6/functional/item:6 (no format) and NNS-UN-005 (ambiguous, resolved for the many-lines reading under c-040). Engine view: there is no upload service in the plants repo (repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend/src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md 'Out of scope': obligations and fulfilments only, no uploads) and the records adapter is Mapper A only (skeleton persistence-and-mapper), so a file-driven route is a model and platform extension, not a page increment — a park under standing ruling 1 as well. The behaviour detail already says 'PARKED, not rejected' with the right citations and the right future shape.

decisions.resolution: Not built in this phase. NNS-UN-042 stays a parked convenience need. If picked up it is an upload-and-extract route feeding the same obligations, which first needs the epic's document-upload exclusion lifted and a plants source to name the documents and their machine-readable format.
decisions.rationale: NNS-UN-042 ('import consignment information from existing documents') is the only source and names neither the documents nor the format (extract.confluence-user-needs existingDocuments conditionsRaw). No plants source imposes a document: the SI matters name none (annex:5/reg:24A(2), reg:26(2)) and the mural reads 'No export cert required' (file:blueprint/region:Export certification; extract.mural:377). Epic EUDPA-407 puts document uploads out of this run, the plants repo has no upload service (sets/high-risk-plants/docs/services.md 'Out of scope') and the records adapter is Mapper A only with 'no document upload' (skeleton persistence-and-mapper). Standing ruling 1: new platform capability plus a source nobody has — parked, not rejected, because the minimum-effort need (annex:6/non-functional/item:10) is genuine. The behaviour detail already says this.
decisions.dissent: GDS judge attributed the decision to Sam. No standing ruling names document import (ruling 3 covers bulk upload; the epic covers document uploads); the panel applied ruling 1, so decidedBy is panel.

decisions.resolution: Not built as an increment of its own.
