decisions.resolution: Parked. No eligibility checker or before-you-start page in this run. NNS-UN-001, 002 and 008 are met inside the journey by a dashboard intro that names the scheme and the three commodity groups and links to GOV.UK guidance only when a real URL exists (a copy leaf, never a '#' link), by commodity-type option hints that quote the SI's timing windows in the SI's own words, and by per-field hints. An in-service 'Is my consignment high-risk?' checker driven by the set-owned commodities service is recorded as a later start-section page, not rejected.
decisions.rationale: All three judges park. The SI places the duty to know whether goods are in scope on the professional operator (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)) and requires nothing of the service by way of guidance; annex 6 lists no guidance function. The mural places guidance outside the service — 'New SPS rules on GOV.UK and Europa.EU' is the Guidance & comms stage (extract.mural guidance-new-sps-rules: 'the journey needs at most a link to GOV.UK guidance rather than in-journey guidance pages') — and 'The board draws no screens'. The commodity list is dynamic and legislation-driven (annex:1/closing-para, phnns-policy.txt:139: 'The list will be dynamic and subject to risk based changes ... the digital solution will need to include the functionality to enable the list to be amended'), so a checker built now would encode a list nobody has settled and would need the wood and potato exclusions that are themselves open (wood-scope-caveats-as-guidance, potato-scope-guidance); standing ruling 1 parks it. The user needs are real (NNS-UN-001 'understand whether my goods are high-risk and subject to a pre or post-movement notification'; NNS-UN-002/008 'understand what information is required ... correctly first time'), which is why this is park, not reject, and why the intro and hints must carry the guidance now. A dead '#' guidance link would be a broken promise, so the link is conditional on a URL in the copy leaf. The intro is new copy (animals' body 'live animals you are importing' is flagged not-to-copy, extract.live-animals:1342, 2224) and carries provisionalCopy; it need not name the territory, and where it does it says Great Britain (c-001, resolved). One correction the law forces on the hints: the Policy section's 'no later than 4 days after date of arrival in GB' (phnns-policy.txt:18) drops the SI's 'before or' (reg 26(1), phnns-policy.txt:290: 'before or no later than four days after the date of their arrival'), so the commodity-type option hints quote reg 24A(1) and reg 26(1) rather than the Policy section's shortened form. The windows are kept out of the dashboard intro so the day counts are written in one journey-copy place that reads the constants ruled under day-one-critical-and-list-volatility (copy functions take the day count as an argument; copy-parity checks arity, not values). The arrivalStatus post-arrival hint ruled at c-031 ('It must be made no later than 4 days after the date of arrival') is correct for that state (already arrived, so 'before' is moot) and stays with c-031.
decisions.dissent: GDS service-design judge wanted the two timing windows spelled out in the dashboard intro as well as on the commodity-type hints. Lost on the day-one-critical-and-list-volatility constraint: the day counts are written in one journey-copy place reading the constants, and the commodity-type page (the first page after Start) is where the trader chooses the group the window applies to. The engineering judge's provisional href to today's GOV.UK plant-import guidance is carried as a copy-pass option on the guidanceUrl leaf, not as a hard-coded link.

decisions.resolution: Parked as a copy and value-list input only, with no first-pass change. The SI data list (annex 5, reg 24A(2) and reg 26(2)) already fixes what is collected — the previous scheme cannot add or remove a matter — so the pre-2021 scheme and the NI/RoI services can only refine page copy, the potato intended-use options and the identification-number and commodity-code formats, all of which the spec leaves as free text with validationRaw 'none given'. A precedent-driven change lands later as a copy-pair or lib/validate edit, never a model change. Needed: the pre-2021 national notification scheme's data list and the NI/RoI notification screens, obtained by policy or design research before the copy pass.
decisions.rationale: All three judges park. Standing ruling 1: a source nobody could read is parked. The policy paper asserts continuity — 'The information captured by PHNSS will be the same as was required under the previous notification system but with some additional requirements (see annex 2)' (section:policy/para:5, phnns-policy.txt:15) — and precedent — 'Similar notification systems are used in Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland' (section:summary/para:6, phnns-policy.txt:9; section:legal-basis/para:1, phnns-policy.txt:28 'This is understood to be the basis for the schemes in Northern Ireland and RoI') — without reproducing either, and its own general question 1 asks 'Does APHA still have copies of the SOPs/Handbook instructions related to the previous national notification scheme?' (phnns-policy.txt:83), so the policy team owes the answer. Annex 2 restates the SI's matters, and standing ruling 4 makes the SI authoritative on WHAT, so the first pass loses nothing in scope, only in copy and formats. The spec already tracks the gaps a precedent would fill: potatoIntendedUse (no options in any source; radios once policy supplies a list), supplierIdentificationNumber / producerIdentificationNumber / cropIdentificationNumber (no issuing register named) and commodityCode (a format factory is a later lib/validate addition) — copy-pair and lib/validate edits under the controller contract, so nothing about the first-pass model waits on the precedents.

decisions.resolution: Adopted as a standing build constraint on every increment: (1) every commodity-type, category, genus and origin list is data behind the set-owned commodities service, never an obligation or copy literal; (2) the two statutory timing windows are single named constants — POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL = 2 (reg 24A(1)) and PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL = 4 (reg 26(1)) — exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and read by the lateness derivation and by any hint that names a window, so no other copy of the number exists; (3) the England / Great Britain wording and the authority names are copy leaves. A reissued policy paper is then a data or copy change, never a model change. The go-live date and who re-runs the digest are delivery notes outside the spec.
decisions.rationale: All three judges adopt. 'The PHNNS has been identified as a day 1 critical need' (section:summary/para:5, phnns-policy.txt:8) with no date given; the paper is a Version 1 draft with draft SI text; the commodity list 'will be dynamic and subject to risk based changes this will require changes to legislation and the digital solution will need to include the functionality to enable to the list to be amended' (annex:1/closing-para, phnns-policy.txt:139) and annex 6 asks for 'easy maintenance of Commodities in scope; Genus & species in scope' (annex:6/functional/item:4, phnns-policy.txt:348-350); the mural blueprint is 'Alpha Phase Confirmed - Update as Required'. A statutory list that will change by regulation must not be hard-coded, and a window that may be renumbered must live in one place. The engine already gives the shape and the spec already points this way: set-owned-commodities-service (adopted) holds the lists with obligations/whitelists.test.js pinning every allow-list against it (skeleton set-owned-services-seam); timing-window-enforcement-and-late-highlight derives lateness from arrivalDate, commodityType and dateOfNotification with the two windows as inputs; date-and-time-entry already places the journey's bounds helper beside the arrival-details feature; welsh-copy-seam makes every user-facing string a copy leaf and copy-parity checks function arity, not values, so a copy function may take the day count as an argument. Nothing here needs a policy answer and every part is cheap and sourced, so under standing ruling 1 it is adopted rather than parked.

decisions.resolution: Adopt at page level: every plants page ships the fit-spec axe check on its initial and validation-error states plus the Lighthouse accessibility floor, and the axe tag list is widened from the two WCAG 2.0 tags to ['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa','wcag22aa'] so the machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules actually run. The manual WCAG 2.2 audit and this service's own accessibility statement are parked, not built, and the footer's accessibility link is routed through the gated chrome extra.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:1 'System is accessible (WCAG2.2AA)' (phnns-policy.txt:361) names no auditor and no statement. The buildable part is already adopted: feature-test-conventions-and-axe (skeleton fit-spec-conventions: AxeBuilder on initial AND error state, serious/critical fail) and lighthouse-audit-per-page (skeleton lighthouse-expectations: accessibility floor 0.70). The spec's own sentence 'axe tags cover WCAG 2.1' is wrong: sets/high-risk-plants/docs/add-a-page.md:299 and the skeleton both build axe with withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa']), which in axe-core are the WCAG 2.0 tags; 2.1 and 2.2 rules carry wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa and are skipped by the two-tag list. The installed axe-core 4.12.1 (package.json:95; node_modules/axe-core/axe.js carries the wcag22aa tag) supports the wider list, so the widening is a one-line sourced change the engine judge confirms is buildable; it diverges from animals' two-tag list (live-animals add-a-page.md:280, origin.fit.spec.js:61) on the strength of a plants source, which standing ruling 5 requires and annex:6 supplies. govuk-frontend 6.x components and the journey shape (save-and-return, address-book-picker, cya-change-round-trip, the fixed footer and confirmation help block) serve most of the 2.2-only criteria by design, but no source names who runs the manual audit or writes the statement, and shared/layout.njk:122 links 'Accessibility statement' to the generic https://www.gov.uk/help/accessibility-statement — a placeholder of the kind c-032 and the chrome-placeholders-and-service-name extra (gate sam) already track. Standing ruling 1 parks the audit and statement.
decisions.dissent: All three judges adopt. Judges 1 (policy) and 2 (GDS) left the axe tag list untouched on the spec's premise that wcag2a/wcag2aa already cover WCAG 2.1; that premise lost because axe-core's tags are version-specific — verified against add-a-page.md:299, the skeleton fit-spec-conventions text and the installed axe-core — so the engine judge's one-line widening is adopted.

decisions.resolution: Adopt: the codebase side of 'meets GDS standards' is delivered by the adopted engine conventions — govuk-frontend 6.x components only, one thing per page, error summary, task-list hub, check your answers, confirmation panel and the Alpha phase banner matching the mural's confirmed phase. The Service Standard assessment is a programme event outside the spec and is recorded as such. A plain-English sweep of every same-as-animals string for animal nouns is added as a rider; the one known instance (countryOfOrigin error copy) is already conflict c-027 and is ruled there, not here.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:2 'Meets GDS standards' (phnns-policy.txt:362) is unqualified and no source names an assessment or phase. The mural's 'Alpha Phase Confirmed - Update as Required' sticky (file:blueprint, extract.mural.json:521) agrees with the engine's Alpha banner (layout-chrome). Design System conformance is already adopted through govuk-toolbox-only, single-question-heading-convention, layout-chrome and error-summary-and-http-400, so every page increment inherits it and nothing buildable remains. Judge 2's copy finding is real — journey-spec.json:1869-1870 carries errorCopy 'Select the country where the animal originates from' and the animals Welsh — but conflicts.json c-027 already records exactly that defect with a provisional pick for the copy pass, so ruling it under D7 would collide with the docket that owns c-027; the panel cross-references it and generalises the sweep instead.
decisions.dissent: All three judges adopt. Judge 2 (GDS) also proposed rewriting countryOfOrigin's errorCopy to 'Select the country of origin', dropping errorCopyCy and setting provisionalCopy here; that lost because conflicts.json c-027 already carries this exact defect for its own docket to rule, and a second ruling on the same field from D7 would collide with it — the sweep rule keeps the finding without the collision.

decisions.resolution: Park the governance items — lawful basis, privacy notice content and URL, retention of drafts and submitted notifications — because the policy paper supplies none of them and the panel must not invent them. What the first pass owes GDPR it already does: it collects only the Annex 5 matters plus the paper's Common Data (Article 9(7) OCR is the ceiling), scopes every record to the Defra ID organisation, takes no document upload, and keeps the footer Privacy link, whose destination resolves under the gated chrome extra.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:3 'Meets GDPR requirements' (phnns-policy.txt:363) is the only mention; the paper gives no lawful basis, privacy notice or retention period (behaviour detail: 'says nothing about record retention periods'). Personal data held is the Common Data set (phnns-policy.txt:162-166: name of person making entry, contact number, contact address, contact email), the consignor name and address (annex:5/reg:26(2)(f)) and the Defra ID user — nothing beyond the paper's list, and section:legal-basis/para:1 (phnns-policy.txt:28, Article 9(7) OCR 'to the extent strictly necessary') is the ceiling. shared/layout.njk:114 links 'Privacy' to https://www.gov.uk/help/privacy-notice, the generic GOV.UK notice — a placeholder in the family chrome-placeholders-and-service-name (gate sam) already covers. Retention is a backend and data-protection matter the frontend cannot express: the plants backend stamps expireAt = created + ttl days only outside production and returns early when isProd (NotificationService.java:328-334; NotificationAggregate.expireAt 'null in prod'), so production retention is undefined — precisely the policy answer nobody has. The address-book inline copy on contactAddress is the same data held twice by one controller, a retention question rather than a new category. Standing ruling 1 parks all of it.
decisions.dissent: All three judges park. Judge 2 (GDS) wrote the lawful basis into the record as 'expected: legal obligation under the draft SI'; that guess is dropped because naming a lawful basis the paper does not state is exactly the invention standing ruling 1 forbids — the item is parked for policy to answer.

decisions.resolution: Park under Sam's standing ruling on users and sign-in models. Annex 6 item 4 speaks only of internal users, who this frontend does not serve; the notifier keeps the Defra ID OIDC sign-in, stub session with auth enforced, and organisation-scoped records exactly as already adopted, and nothing more is built. Whether policy accepts Defra ID as the external identity, and the mural's 'Register for new [GB product]' registration stage, are out of this phase.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:4 'System is secure (userid & password to access for internal users)' (phnns-policy.txt:364) names internal users only, and the paper says nothing about how the professional operator (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)) signs in, so the SI imposes no registration on the notifier beyond being the operator who must notify. The frontend side is built and adopted: stub-mode-and-sign-in (skeleton session-cookies-and-stub-mode — Defra ID OIDC /auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-in-oidc, /auth/organisation in real mode; /auth/stub-sign-in with 'auth is still enforced' in STUB_MODE) and dashboard-listing (scoped to the session organisation, no org -> empty list). Internal userid/password access is another product. The mural's registration stage (extract.mural.json:298 'Register for new [GB product]'; :715 notes the bracketed name is a placeholder) is a sign-in-model question. Standing ruling 2 parks users, sign-in models and plant-operator registration with decidedBy sam.

decisions.resolution: Adopt the journey's share of 24x7 availability, which the engine already delivers: save-and-return, recoverable-save and stale-action banners that keep the user's answers, a synchronous submit with no long work, and a late-notification derivation computed in Europe/London so a submission at any hour is judged on the right calendar day. Nothing in the journey may gate submission by time of day. Peak-load targets and a plants k6 suite are parked as infrastructure follow-ons; platform availability is the CDP SLA.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:6 'Available 24x7' (phnns-policy.txt:366) is unqualified; the SI counts its windows in days with no hour-of-day cut-off (annex:5/reg:24A(1) 'at least two days before'; reg:26(1) 'no later than four days after'), so the service must accept a notification whenever the operator makes it. nns-un-009 (extract.confluence-user-needs.json:462 'complete my notification process dependably whenever required') and nns-un-026 (:586-589, whose own implication says it 'bears on infrastructure and performance testing rather than journey shape') restate this; the mural's '59k (26% of Plants / 5% of total imports)' (extract.mural.json:416-419) 'sizes the service but does not change the journey model' and is an annual volume, not a peak. The journey-side behaviours are adopted already: save-and-return, recoverable-save-and-stale-action, declaration-and-submit-gate and live-access-synchronous-submission (submitJourney -> records.finalise -> SUBMITTED before the confirmation renders), and lateNotificationIndicator's derivation is 'computed once at submission in Europe/London' (journey-spec.json:2812ff). A find for k6 across the tests repo and both frontends, excluding node_modules, returns nothing, and no source gives a peak target, so under standing ruling 1 the suite is parked.

decisions.resolution: Park the live Welsh service: the first release ships English-only with html lang en, the copy seam stays exactly as adopted so every plants string lands in both locale files at once, no Welsh is invented, and the runtime locale switch is not built because it is new engine capability and no translation has been commissioned. The follow-on is written into the behaviour in full so it can be cut as one extra the day a Welsh Language Standards owner and translation exist.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:7 'Available in English & Welsh language' (phnns-policy.txt:367) is the paper's own requirement and outranks every other source, so it cannot be rejected. Nothing that meets it is buildable now: shared/copy.js:15-16 copyFor(locales, locale = 'en') is only ever called with the default, and its docblock (copy.js:7-9) says selection 'plugs in via the locale argument when it is' commissioned; welsh-copy-seam records 'no locale toggle, cookie or lang attribute exists in animals or the plants engine'; every cy file is MACHINE-DRAFT that 'must not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off' (skeleton tripwire-copy-parity); the reconciler brief forbids inventing Welsh (RECONCILER-BRIEF.md:140-143), so variant and plants-only copy has none. Wiring a switch touches kit.base, the layout, the session and every controller's copyFor call — a model extension parked under standing ruling 1. Shipping half-Welsh machine drafts behind a toggle would serve Welsh speakers worse than a clean English-only release with lang en, which is why the seam is kept and the toggle is not. The paper does not say whether English-only is acceptable for a first release, so that is recorded against the release rather than resolved.
decisions.dissent: All three judges park. Judge 2 (GDS) also wanted a new extra welsh-locale-and-translation (gate sam, anchor end) so the requirement is not lost; that lost because an extra gated on Sam but BLOCKED on a translation nobody has commissioned would halt the build loop for a decision Sam cannot take alone — the parked behaviour is the record standing ruling 1 asks for, and it now carries Judge 2's full five-step plan so the extra can be cut verbatim when translation exists.

decisions.resolution: Adopt: the first pass meets the requirement by asking only the Annex 5 matters plus the paper's Common Data, hiding questions outside the commodity's scope, save-and-return, address-book picks and change-from-CYA. Article 9(7) OCR makes this a ceiling as well as a goal — every question must trace to the SI or the Common Data list and no increment may add one that does not; any future optional question carries '(optional)' and never gates readiness. The three effort-savers stay parked under their own behaviours, bulk upload by Sam's ruling.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:10 'Minimise effort and potential disruption to traders' (phnns-policy.txt:370); section:reporting-requirements/para:2/item:2 'not overly onerous to trade' (:68); nns-un-004 'simple ... minimal effort', bold in the source (extract.confluence-user-needs.json:429-433). Legally, section:legal-basis/para:1 — Article 9(7) OCR allows notification only 'to the extent strictly necessary for the organisation of the official controls' (:28) — so every question must trace to annex:5/reg:24A(2) or reg:26(2), or to the paper's Common Data list (phnns-policy.txt:162-166); anything else is both extra effort and beyond the power the scheme rests on. Adopted behaviours already deliver the effort side: proportionate-questions-by-scope, scope-and-wipe-on-exit, single-question-heading-convention, save-and-return, address-book-picker, cya-change-round-trip, amend-before-submitting. The three savers are OUT in the brief (RECONCILER-BRIEF.md:69-72) and parked under their own behaviours — bulk-upload by standing ruling 3, reuse-previous-consignment and import-from-existing-documents per the brief. Judge 2's optional-question rider is GOV.UK Design System convention: consignmentNumber is the one optional obligation (c-003 — labelled 'Consignment number (optional)', hub row Optional for wood, never gates readiness) and already follows it, so the rider binds later pages; its phrasing 'nothing outside annex:5 may be mandatory' is corrected because the Common Data contact obligations come from annex:6, not annex:5, and are required.
decisions.dissent: All three judges adopt. Judge 2 (GDS) phrased the rider as 'no question outside the annex:5 data list may be mandatory'; that wording lost because the paper's Common Data list (annex:6) is also a source and its contact obligations are required — the ceiling is annex:5 plus Common Data, as Judge 1 framed it.

decisions.resolution: Park. 'Sustainable' is a single unqualified word in the only source that uses it, nothing in the journey depends on it, and the panel adopts no reading; the behaviour stays so the Annex 6 list is complete, and policy is asked what was meant before anything hangs on it.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/non-functional/item:5 'Sustainable' (phnns-policy.txt:365) has no gloss anywhere in the policy paper, the Confluence extracts or the mural; the requirements workbooks that might qualify it are the SharePoint sources no extractor could read. Standing ruling 1: a policy answer nobody has is parked, not rejected (rejecting would drop it from the Annex 6 completeness record) and not built (there is nothing to build). Judge 2's maintainability reading is not adopted as a reading — inventing a meaning is what standing ruling 1 forbids — but the fact that the M0 hygiene extras (dependabot-frontend, dependabot-backend, docs-drift-sweep, all present in backlog-extras.json) would already serve that reading is worth recording so no increment is derived from it whichever way policy answers.
decisions.dissent: All three judges park. Judge 2 (GDS) recorded a 'provisional reading: maintainable and supportable'; that lost as a reading under standing ruling 1 (no invented requirement), though its observation about the hygiene extras is kept as fact.

decisions.resolution: Adopt the notifier journey's share of the eight metrics, which the spec already carries: coded commodityType, category, genus and ISO countryOfOrigin for metrics 1-3, and the record envelope's createdAt and submittedAt (dateOfNotification) for metric 6; the journey measures nothing and adds no question for MI. The definition of 'time taken per notification' stays a parked policy question with created-to-submitted as the interim reading. One verified gap is fixed by a new extra: the plants backend's list projection carries no submittedAt, so the dashboard's Date submitted row is empty in real mode and metric 6 cannot be read from the list.
decisions.rationale: section:reporting-requirements/para:3/item:1-8 lists the eight (phnns-policy.txt:72-77) and para:4 says 'The information does not have to necessarily come directly from the PHNNS digital solution' (:81), which settles that the journey owes data, not measurement; annex:6/functional/item:7 'Facilitate management information and report generation' (:354). Coded values are in the spec (countryOfOrigin input.service 'stores ISO 3166-1 alpha-2'; category, genus, commodityType as input.values), and dateOfNotification is SYSTEM_POPULATED 'date-time stamped at submitJourney (records.finalise)' with displayedOn 'dashboard card Date submitted; also ... the MI metric time taken per notification' (journey-spec.json:2732-2745). Article 9(7) OCR forbids adding notifier questions for reporting's sake. Metrics 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 are inspector-side and OUT in the brief. Judge 3's 'RESOLVED: wall-clock created to submitted' overreaches — the paper frames the metric as trader burden (para:2/item:2) and defines nothing — so the definition is parked and the journey records both ends. Judge 2's gap is verified and wider than stated: the single-record read (GET /notifications/{ref}/fulfilments -> NotificationFulfilmentsView.getSubmittedAt) and every transition response (NotificationAggregate, which has submittedAt) do carry the stamp, so confirmation and CYA are fine; but the list (GET /notifications -> NotificationPageResponse of NotificationView, whose fields are referenceNumber, concurrencyToken, status, created — plants-backend NotificationView.java:31-35) has no submittedAt, which is why services/persistence/records/real/marshal/list-item.js:32 hardcodes submittedAt: null. Animals has the identical hole (animals list-item.js:32), so fixing it diverges from animals in adapter code only, grounded in section:reporting-requirements/para:3/item:6 and the dateOfNotification displayedOn — standing ruling 5 satisfied. The fix spans the plants backend and frontend, so it lands on one branch name in both repos (rule 2).
decisions.dissent: All three judges adopt. Judge 3 (engine) wanted the metric's definition RESOLVED as wall-clock createdAt to submittedAt and proposed no fix for the list; that lost because the paper defines nothing and the panel must not define policy's metric — created-to-submitted stays the interim reading — and because the list gap Judge 2 found is real and, on inspection of the backend types, sits in the NotificationView projection rather than only in the frontend marshal Judge 2 named, so the extra is adopted in the verified two-repo shape.

decisions.resolution: Park under Sam's standing ruling on users and access models. Parity of internal access for Defra Policy, Scottish Government and the Forestry Commission is a multi-organisation user model for the regulator product, wholly outside the notifier frontend; the journey owes it only the full submitted record with no organisation-based withholding, which it already persists, and its one touchpoint — the confirmation naming all three competent authorities without preferring one — is already in the spec.
decisions.rationale: annex:6/functional/item:11 'Provides Defra Policy, Scottish Government and Forestry Commission with the same level of access to the data in the system as APHA' (phnns-policy.txt:358) and section:summary/para:4; section:policy/para:7 makes APHA, FC and Scottish Government the competent authorities who receive the notification. Every consequence is internal-side (regulator-views, inspector-recording, analyst-export — all OUT per RECONCILER-BRIEF.md:69-72) and on who those users are, which standing ruling 2 puts out of this phase with decidedBy sam. The engine has no internal-user role or cross-organisation read — dashboard-listing is 'scoped to the session organisation (no org -> empty list)' and the only role is the stub Farmer/scope user (skeleton session-cookies-and-stub-mode) — so building it would be a new product surface. The confirmation page body already says 'the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may carry out a spot check' (journey-spec.json:1048), so the trader sees one service whichever authority acts. The paper itself leaves the integration open: 'How will PHNSS interact with relevant Forestry Commission and Scottish Government IT systems?' (phnns-policy.txt:88) and 'Impacts on enforcement bodies' TBC (:61).

decisions.resolution: The dashboard increment rewrites copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js in the same commit as the first feature folder; the two restore extras (restore-copy-convention-tripwire, restore-copy-parity-tripwire) are withdrawn and their detail folds into the dashboard increment's plan. The flow/section-captions pair still joins copy-parity with wire-section-captions.
decisions.rationale: Under the batch orchestrator every increment is its own ticket, branch and PR, and the PR's CI runs npm test. A dashboard PR that leaves both tripwires red can never merge, so the restore cannot be a later increment. The build handover (workareas/shared/high-risk-plants-digest/BUILD-HANDOVER.md, 'What will stop the run') anticipates folding the restore into the same increment; the orchestrator applied it on 2026-09-06 and Sam has not yet confirmed — supersede this decision to reverse it.
